prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” roofer for everyone — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, roof type, insurance situation, and your priorities (price, speed, warranty). I can help you find the best roofer in Denver for hail damage by walking you through what to look for and how to compare contractors, or I can search for specific local companies if you give me your ZIP code (I can’t browse the web myself without that input).

Quick questions so I can tailor recommendations:
- Is this residential or commercial?
- Do you already have an insurance claim open?
- What ZIP code or neighborhood in Denver?
- Any deadline (e.g., visible leaks, urgent repairs)?

How to find the best hail-damage roofer in Denver (step-by-step)
1. Start with reputable search sources
   - Google Business listings, Yelp, Angi, Nextdoor, BBB, and local Facebook groups. Look for firms with many recent, positive reviews about hail work and insurance claims.
2. Verify credentials
   - Colorado roofer license (verify locally), general liability and workers’ comp insurance, and local building-permit experience.
   - Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc.) — these indicate training and enhanced warranties.
3. Prefer contractors with storm/hail-claim experience
   - They should understand insurance estimates (Xactimate), supplementing claims, and meet adjusters. Ask how many hail claims they do per season.
4. Get at least 3 written estimates
   - Ask for detailed line items, materials, proposed warranty, and whether the price includes permits and disposal.
   - Prefer Xactimate-style estimates or itemized bids you can compare.
5. Ask key questions
   - Will you handle insurance communications or just the work?
   - Which manufacturer/warranty will you provide (material vs. workmanship)?
   - Who will perform the work (company crews vs. subcontractors)?
   - What is the timeline and cleanup plan?
6. Check references and photos
   - Ask for recent local project photos and references you can call (especially other hail repairs).
7. Watch for red flags
   - “Storm chasers” pressuring to sign immediately, very large upfront deposits, no written estimate or contract, no local address, poor communication, vague warranty.
8. Confirm permits and inspections
   - Roofing projects often require permits; the contractor should obtain them and pass local inspections.
9. Compare warranties and follow-up
   - Material warranty (from manufacturer) vs. workmanship warranty (from contractor). Get both in writing.

What I can do next
- If you give me your ZIP code and whether you want contractors who handle insurance, I’ll list prominent Denver-area hail/heavy-storm roofers to consider and what to ask each of them.
- If you already have 2–3 bids, paste them here and I’ll help compare and point out likely gaps or overcharges.

If you want immediate names right now, tell me your ZIP and whether residential/commercial and insurance-handling preference.
